maxwelllink.description: Use this family for intents about coupled electromagnetic and molecular simulation workflows, including MaxwellLink input setup, socket-linked drivers, and local or HPC job execution.

meep.description: Use this family for intents about FDTD Maxwell-wave simulations, photonic device modeling, and electromagnetic field spectrum analysis.

lammps.description: Route requests about classical molecular dynamics, force-field driven atomistic modeling, and large-scale parallel particle simulations to this package family.

qutip.description: Routes requests about numerical quantum dynamics, Lindblad open-system solvers, operator-state representations, and quantum optics modeling in Python.

psi4.description: Use this family for molecular quantum chemistry intents involving ab initio electronic structure methods and Psi4 job workflows.

pyscf.description: Route intents about first-principles electronic-structure chemistry in Python, including SCF and correlated wavefunction methods for molecules and materials, to this package family.

gromacs.description: Use this route for atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, force-field based system preparation, production runs, and trajectory analysis in biomolecular or soft-matter studies.

packmol.description: Use this family for software that prepares initial molecular simulation structures through geometric packing constraints before dynamics runs.

bloqade.description: Use this family for neutral-atom quantum programming, pulse-level control, and compilation or simulation tasks targeting QuEra-style Rydberg platforms.

arc.description: Routes atomic-physics and quantum-optics requests about Rydberg atom structure, interactions, and transition calculations for alkali and alkaline-earth species.

pylcp.description: Use this family for AMO laser-cooling modeling tasks involving optical Bloch equation construction, atom or molecule internal-state Hamiltonians, laser beam setups, and magnetic-field-dependent force calculations.

molecool.description: Use this family for atomic, molecular, and optical physics tasks focused on molecular laser cooling, light-matter dynamics, and spectroscopy-informed trapping optimization.

atomsmltr.description: Use this family for cold-atom physics simulations involving atom-light interactions, laser beam setups, magnetic trapping fields, and motional dynamics.

astropy.description: Use this family for observational astronomy and astrophysics tasks involving celestial coordinates, time standards, physical units, FITS metadata, and cosmological calculations.

photutils.description: Use this family for astronomy workflows centered on extracting and measuring sources in 2D telescope images via aperture, PSF, and segmentation-based photometry.

ccdproc.description: Use for astronomy workflows focused on CCD detector calibration and reduction of raw optical or infrared imaging frames into science-ready data products.

specutils.description: Use this family for astronomy tasks focused on one-dimensional spectral data, spectral line analysis, continuum estimation, and wavelength-domain processing.

yt.description: Use this family for requests about analyzing and visualizing multidimensional simulation fields, meshes, and particles in scientific datasets.

swift.description: Routes to astrophysical and cosmological particle-simulation codes centered on gravity and SPH hydrodynamics at extreme scale.

amuse.description: Use this family for requests about orchestrating astrophysical codes into unified multi-physics simulation pipelines for computational astronomy.

enzo-e.description: Route requests about adaptive mesh astrophysical or cosmological fluid simulations on large HPC systems, especially Enzo-E or Cello based workflows.

pynbody.description: Routes astronomy simulation-analysis queries involving cosmological particle snapshots, halo measurements, and AMR hydrodynamics across common astrophysical code outputs.

lightkurve.description: Use this family for space-telescope photometric time-series workflows focused on Kepler and TESS light curves, target pixel files, detrending, period searches, and transit analysis.

exoplanet.description: Route requests about Bayesian exoplanet data analysis, orbital parameter estimation, and probabilistic modeling of stellar light curves or radial velocities.

celerite2.description: Routes requests about scalable one-dimensional Gaussian process kernels, fast GP inference, and celerite-style time-series regression for astronomy and related sequential scientific data.

batman.description: Routes queries about exoplanet transit light-curve generation and fitting, especially fast forward models with limb-darkening parameterizations in observational astronomy.

starry.description: Route intents about astrophysical light curve forward modeling, spherical harmonic surface maps, and star planet transit or eclipse mapping to this package.

rdkit.description: Route chemistry and drug-discovery intents here when users mention molecular structures, fingerprints, descriptors, reaction SMARTS, or substructure matching.

openbabel.description: Use for requests on translating chemical structure files, SMARTS substructure queries, and coordinate generation in cheminformatics pipelines.

deepchem.description: Best for requests on cheminformatics workflows, molecular ML models, and deep-learning pipelines for drug, materials, quantum, or biology tasks.

openff-toolkit.description: Use this family for intents about OpenFF SMIRNOFF force field typing, parameter assignment, and direct chemical perception in molecular simulation preparation.

datamol.description: Route small-molecule cheminformatics requests here, especially RDKit Mol-centric tasks involving cleaning, featurization, conformers, and conversion between common molecular representations and file formats.

nwchem.description: Routes intents about ab initio quantum chemistry and large-scale electronic structure workflows, especially DFT, wavefunction, and parallel molecular simulation tasks.

xtb.description: Routes user intents about semiempirical electronic-structure calculations, fast geometry optimization, and molecular property prediction in the xTB and GFN tight-binding family.

dftd4.description: Use for quantum-chemistry requests involving D4 London dispersion corrections to DFT energies, gradients, Hessians, pairwise terms, or periodic calculations.

openmm.description: Use this family for atomistic molecular dynamics, force-field-driven simulations, and GPU-accelerated biophysical modeling tasks.

hoomd-blue.description: Use this family for particle-based simulation intents centered on soft matter, molecular dynamics, and hard-particle Monte Carlo workflows.

espresso.description: Routes user intents about coarse-grained molecular dynamics, soft-matter many-particle simulations, and mesoscale interaction models controlled through Python scripts.

cantera.description: Routes questions about reacting-chemistry and combustion simulations using kinetics mechanisms, thermodynamic states, transport models, flames, and reactor networks.

rmg-py.description: Routes queries about automated chemical reaction mechanism generation, gas-phase kinetics, and thermochemistry estimation workflows centered on RMG and Arkane.

chempy.description: Use this family for chemistry computation tasks involving reaction systems, equilibrium solvers, rate expressions, and physicochemical property formulas.

thermo.description: Routes intents about chemical thermophysical properties, vapor liquid equilibrium, and equation of state flash modeling for pure compounds and mixtures.

chemicals.description: Use this package for CAS-based chemical property lookup, thermodynamic correlation methods, and flash or equilibrium utilities in process and unit-operation modeling.

wrf.description: Route requests here for WRF ARW workflows involving namelists, WPS preprocessing, physics configuration, and time evolving regional atmosphere simulations.

cesm.description: Use this for coupled climate and Earth system model setup, case configuration, compilation, and production runs.

mpas-model.description: Routes earth-system modeling intents covering MPAS cores, mesh-based dynamical operators, and atmosphere-ocean-seaice-land-ice simulation workflows.

mitgcm.description: Use this family for user intents about numerical ocean atmosphere circulation experiments, geophysical flow dynamics, and coupled ocean sea ice simulations.

mom6.description: Use this family for requests about ocean general circulation, tracer advection, and coupled climate ocean components rather than atmospheric, molecular, or astronomy simulation packages.

cavity-md-ipi.description: Use for chemical-physics routing on cavity-modified molecular dynamics, including photon-coupled nuclei, vibrational strong or ultrastrong coupling, Fabry-Perot multimode effects, and reactive or nonreactive CavMD studies.

biopython.description: Route to this family for DNA or protein sequence workflows, biological file format parsing, alignment tasks, and bioinformatics database access.

pysam.description: Routes intents for high-throughput sequencing file access, indexed genomic region queries, alignment pileups, and variant record manipulation via HTSlib-compatible Python interfaces.

scikit-bio.description: Route requests about biological sequence objects, phylogenetic trees, diversity statistics, and microbiome or community ecology analysis in Python.

snakemake.description: Use this family for intents about authoring Snakefiles, orchestrating rule driven workflows, and scaling scientific pipelines across heterogeneous compute environments.

nextflow.description: Routes requests about scientific workflow authoring, pipeline execution, and reproducibility across distributed compute backends, especially for bioinformatics and genomics.

scanpy.description: Route requests about single-cell omics analysis pipelines using AnnData, including QC, embedding, clustering, marker discovery, and pseudotime workflows.

anndata.description: Route to this family for intents about AnnData objects, single-cell omics matrix annotation, h5ad or zarr I/O, and Scanpy-scverse data workflows.

scvi-tools.description: Routes requests about probabilistic analysis workflows for single-cell, multimodal, and spatial omics, especially latent embeddings, batch correction, annotation, and deconvolution tasks.

squidpy.description: Use this package for spatial transcriptomics and image-aware single-cell workflows, especially graph-based neighborhood statistics and tissue-section visualization in the scverse ecosystem.

cellrank.description: Use this family for single-cell trajectory questions focused on Markov-based fate mapping, RNA velocity integration, and inference of initial, intermediate, or terminal cell states.

pyfr.description: Routes requests about high-order computational fluid dynamics, conservation-law PDE solvers, and unstructured-grid flow simulation on accelerator hardware.

palabos.description: Routes to mesoscopic CFD and lattice Boltzmann solvers for incompressible, multiphase, and porous-media flow simulation on parallel CPU systems.

fdtdbath-meep.description: Use this family for FDTD-Bath approach simulation of polaritonics, which supports also conventional MEEP calculations

specfem3d-globe.description: Routes to computational seismology and geodynamics workflows centered on forward spectral-element simulation of planetary seismic wavefields.

seissol.description: Route intents about computational seismology, dynamic rupture physics, and high-order PDE solvers for crustal earthquake scenario modeling.

devito.description: Use this family for requests about symbolic stencil PDE modeling, automatic kernel generation, and high-performance finite-difference execution workflows.

sw4.description: Route to computational seismology and geophysical wave-equation solvers focused on high-order finite-difference simulation of elastic and anelastic seismic waves.

neuron.description: Use this family for intents about biophysical neuron simulation, compartmental membrane dynamics, synapses, and NEURON-specific modeling workflows.

pylith.description: Routes queries about computational solid-earth geophysics, especially finite-element modeling of faults, crustal stress evolution, and tectonic deformation in dynamic or quasi-static settings.

brian2.description: Use this family for questions about specifying neuron and synapse equations, simulating spike-based networks, and analyzing neural dynamics with Brian2.

nest-simulator.description: Route to this family for computational neuroscience requests about spiking neuron network modeling, synaptic plasticity, or large-scale event-driven brain simulations.

tvb-root.description: Routes intents for The Virtual Brain ecosystem covering tvb-library simulations, tvb-framework workflows, persistence layers, and neuroscience visual analytics.
